scores.title: Declared diagnosis semantics (faultlab-mechanic-diagnosis/v2-declared-semantics): give the diagnosis Mechanic facts that are already public or recorded, tell it the length limit on repair, and record why no intervention ran. No verdict code or gate changes.
scores.reasons:
EFFECTIVENESS 5/10. BUILD/REVIEW COST 4/10 (10 = cheapest).

What decides dev-5 today. I checked the code:
- The verdict turns on only two model behaviours: returning a valid answer, and naming the one offered option.
- The candidate request never sees the Mechanic's hypothesis. The candidate context carries DiagnosticResult with a fixed explanation (learning.py:259; diagnostics.py:81).
- So a design helps dev-5 only if it cuts the two observed losses: v2e's null request and v2g's 614-character rejection.

Part B (repair turn states max_characters 600 and your_characters 614) is a real, targeted fix for the v2g loss:
- v2f shows the model can shorten when it is asked to repair (743 characters became 428).
- v2g resent identical text only because the repair message (mechanic.py:69-73) drops the limit and says "Correct formatting only... Do not add ... a new hypothesis".
- Historically the format loss is small: 1 of 16 V4-Pro diagnoses (inv-C). It was still 1 of the 2 dev-5 losses.

Part A (kind definitions, C1-C8 meanings, task text, verdict rule) is aimed at the v2e decline. The evidence that information alone moves that choice is weak:
- The existing prompt already says "Request the intervention whose treatment removes the suspected cause and is expected to show zero target violations" (diagnosis.md:5).
- Every dev-5 context already showed control 3/3 and treatment 0/3. I confirmed this in all four rebuilt contexts.
- v2g's own answer said "C6 passes" and still blamed citations.
- The verdict_rule sentence (null means INCONCLUSIVE) may help. But v2e declined because it thought INCONCLUSIVE was the right answer for its hypothesis, so being told that null leads to INCONCLUSIVE may not change its mind.
- About 700 extra tokens could also lengthen hypotheses. Both over-limit answers came from the builds with more text (n=2).

Expected result on dev-5: probably 3 of 4 or better, not reliably 4 of 4. Every step after the Mechanic answer is unchanged.

Part C (a sidecar that separates declined from invalid from requested, and records where proposed_kind came from) adds no effectiveness. It is valuable observability, and it would have prevented the doc error at PRODUCT_NATIVE_V2_RUN_2026-09-29.md:393.

Cost:
- It touches shared agents/mechanic.py and needs a golden byte-identity test for the flag-off path.
- It also touches run_plans, exports and learning.py, and adds a new module and a new record type.
- Its effect cannot be shown at $0. It needs a paid probe, then a live run.
blocking_concerns: The effect on the Mechanic's null-request rate is untested. The current prompt already tells it to pick the zero-violation option, and every dev-5 context already showed 3/3 vs 0/3, so an information-only fix may not move the v2e-type decline. A pre-registered paid probe is needed before claiming it makes the path reliable.
agents/mechanic.py is shared by every plan. The flag-off path must be proved byte-identical against the inv-a rebuilt v2f/v2g first and repair turns before merge.
Even if it works, it leaves the model's veto in place: any decline or second format failure still drops a reproduced, reduced source at learning.py:250.

scores.title: Fixed-default intervention when the Mechanic names none (protocol faultlab-diagnosis-selection/v2-fixed-default)
scores.reasons:
EFFECTIVENESS 9/10. BUILD/REVIEW COST 5/10 (10 = cheapest).

This is the only design that removes both observed dev-5 losses by construction instead of by persuasion.

Why it works on dev-5:
- In all four dev-5 runs the retained recipe had exactly one option, remove_primitive:0.
- Reduction had already observed control 3 valid / 3 violations and treatment 3 fresh / 3 valid / 0 violations. I re-read this from inv-a/*-diagnosis-context.json, and every reduction was LOCALLY_MINIMAL.
- designer-effectiveness/fixed_default_check.json shows the default would have picked the recorded options: intervention-e91961428eedb56e8fa30e3b for v2e and intervention-828103e0598f48f8675994a5 for v2g.
- v2d, v2f and v2g-dev6 are unchanged, because the default equals the Mechanic's pick.
- The eligibility rule is computed before the answer is read, so no model output can steer it.

Nothing downstream loses input:
- The candidate request never gets the diagnosis hypothesis. It gets DiagnosticResult with a fixed explanation (learning.py:259; diagnostics.py:81).
- It gets the same fresh intervention evidence either way.
- run_interventions checks nothing about proposal_ref or hypothesis beyond the dataclass, and a 454-character fixed hypothesis fits Text 600.

Remaining risk sits in fixed code and the agent, not the Mechanic:
- The fresh control must repeat 3/3. Native-v2 fresh interventions were SUPPORTED 3 of 3.
- A candidate followed 10 of 11 POLICY_GAP diagnoses, and the one miss was a budget stop.
- So the expected dev-5 result is about 4 of 4 POLICY_GAP and a candidate, against 2 of 4 today.
- It is not 10 because the fresh-repeat evidence is n=3, and because the owner may reject it.

The effect can be proved fully offline at $0, deterministically. Designs 1 and 3 cannot be.

Limits:
- It does nothing for reference-agent sources, whose losses were fresh-control failures (9 of 14 INCONCLUSIVE interventions), not declines (0 of 19).
- It does nothing for MechanicContextUnfit refusals.

Cost:
- The code is moderate: an elif branch in lab/diagnosis.py, plan plumbing, a selection record, an export key and a UI label.
- Review is heavy because it is a written-protocol change. The Mechanic loses its veto over the fixed experiment (experiment-protocol.md:82-83; diagnosis.py:1).
- It could be combined with Design 1's Part B (repair limit) and one merged sidecar record. That combination would also improve records without confounding the effect.
blocking_concerns: It needs the owner's explicit acceptance of the spec amendment to experiment-protocol.md:82-83 and of the diagnosis.py:1 design-rule change, because it removes the Mechanic's veto. It must not ship without that.

After a LOCALLY_MINIMAL reduction, POLICY_GAP becomes nearly automatic, so diagnosis stops filtering sources and depends on reduction repeating. Every report and dashboard must split results by selected_by (MECHANIC / FIXED_DEFAULT / NONE), never count a fixed default as a Mechanic success, and never pool POLICY_GAP rates with those from older plans.

It edits lab/diagnosis.py, which sits next to the verdict code. Tests must prove the selection=None path is byte-identical (same context hash, same runner calls, same records) for every saved plan before merge.

scores.title: Minimal change: one declared, fixed 'diagnosis_guide' block (kind definitions, public check meanings, task text, length rule) added to Mechanic diagnosis requests in new Learn plans only
scores.reasons:
EFFECTIVENESS 4/10. BUILD/REVIEW COST 7/10 (10 = cheapest).

It works on the same lever as Design 1's Part A: correcting the citation misreading so the Mechanic stops declining. It shares the same weak evidence:
- The existing diagnosis prompt already tells the Mechanic to request the zero-violation option (diagnosis.md:5).
- Every dev-5 context already showed 3/3 vs 0/3.
- v2g already stated "C6 passes" and still blamed citations.

It is likely to improve hypothesis quality. But the hypothesis is not used downstream: the candidate request carries only DiagnosticResult's fixed explanation (learning.py:259). So better hypotheses do not make the path to a candidate more reliable.

Its length fix is soft and misses the actual v2g failure:
- The first turn already carried "<=600" in the system prompt.
- The repair instruction still says "Correct formatting only... Do not add ... a new hypothesis" and still omits the limit (mechanic.py:73).
- The new sentence sits in the resent first user message, about 10k tokens earlier. This is weaker than Design 1's max_characters/your_characters in the repair turn itself.
- The block's 631 extra tokens could modestly raise over-length risk.

Expected result on dev-5: somewhere between 2 of 4 and 4 of 4, and unmeasured.

Strengths:
- The cheapest to build and review: a wrapper module, run_plans plumbing and 3 lines in learning.py.
- mechanic.py, diagnosis.py and the referee are untouched.
- It has the cleanest experimental hygiene: a pre-registered paid probe of about $2-5 that tests only the Mechanic's reading, with no episodes.
- It is a good follow-up experiment for hypothesis quality. It is not a reliability fix.
blocking_concerns: Nothing shows it changes the null-request rate or over-length rate. It cannot be called a reliability fix until the pre-registered paid probe (section C of its test plan) shows the change.
It does not address the v2g failure mode. The repair turn still omits the 600 limit and still says not to add a new hypothesis, so an identical resend remains possible.
It leaves the model's veto in place, so any decline or double format failure still drops a reproduced, reduced source at learning.py:250.

scores.title: Declared diagnosis semantics (faultlab-mechanic-diagnosis/v2-declared-semantics): give the diagnosis Mechanic facts that are already public or recorded, tell it the length limit on repair, and record why no intervention ran. No verdict code or gate changes.
scores.reasons:
I checked the code this design leaves alone (read-only, $0, checks.py not opened).

1. Fixed code still decides the verdict.
- classify_policy_gap (backend/app/referee/diagnostics.py:76-81) reads only the reproduction trials and the fresh intervention result. proposed_kind is only stored.
- Diagnostician.run is not edited (backend/app/lab/diagnosis.py:123-151), nor is the candidate gate `if diagnostic.kind!='POLICY_GAP': continue` (learning.py:250).
- Because referee/diagnostics.py is not edited, checker_hash and PROTOCOL_HASH stay the same.

2. No gate gets easier.
- The 600-character limit, the null path (diagnosis.py:135,145), the invalid-output default (diagnosis.py:149), the 3/3-vs-0/3 fresh rule (diagnostics.py:53-71), the option list and the hard-coded 'removes_violation' prediction are all unchanged.

3. Nothing new about any episode reaches the model.
- The added text is fixed, plus the campaign's task_text. The task text is already bound to the plan (runner.py:87) and already sent to the agent inside the intent (runner.py:165, external_agent.py:315).
- PUBLIC_INVARIANTS (explorer.py:21-30) is public text the Explorer already gets (explorer.py:284).
- The verdict_rule describes referee/diagnostics.py, not checks.py.
- The block goes only to diagnosis requests. Candidate requests get the diagnostic record without the hypothesis (learning.py:259), so the policy author learns nothing new.
- The diagnosis output has no scoring role, so knowing the rule gives the model nothing to exploit.

4. It is honest to declare, and it makes the records more honest.
- The text is frozen in the plan, hashed and checked at Start, and each field is omitted when absent, so old plans keep their bytes.
- The diagnosis_requests record separates a model-chosen kind from the code default. That ambiguity is what produced the false statement at docs/PRODUCT_NATIVE_V2_RUN_2026-09-29.md:393. This is a real integrity gain.

5. Deductions.
- (a) The verdict_rule says a null request means INCONCLUSIVE and that 'Requesting an intervention is not a claim that it will be SUPPORTED'. That nudges the model toward always requesting, which weakens its informal filter. The designer declares this risk openly and offers a variant without the sentence.
- (b) It edits agents/mechanic.py, which every plan shares, behind a flag (the repair message is built at mechanic.py:69-73 today). A flag-off byte-identity golden test is a hard precondition.
- (c) The text 'a check row with passed true means fixed code found that invariant satisfied' depends on PUBLIC_INVARIANTS matching what checks.py implements. Nobody in this review could verify that, because checks.py is off limits.
- (d) Applying it to every Learn plan, including the reference agent, confounds comparisons with past runs. This is a scope choice, not a gate issue.

scores.title: Fixed-default intervention when the Mechanic names none (protocol faultlab-diagnosis-selection/v2-fixed-default)
scores.reasons:
1. What holds up.
- Fixed code still assigns the verdict: classify_policy_gap is unchanged, and every POLICY_GAP still needs fresh trials at 3/3 control and 0/3 treatment (diagnostics.py:53-81).
- The default is chosen before the answer is read, from options named before the model is called (diagnosis.py:125-132). The model cannot steer it.
- The model gets less power, not more, so there is nothing for it to game.
- The design is candid that it amends the written protocol (experiment-protocol.md:82-83) and needs the owner's acceptance.

2. On the judging criteria it fails in several ways.
- It makes the diagnosis step easier to pass.
  - Today POLICY_GAP needs a valid 3/3 reproduction, a valid Mechanic answer that requests an option, and a SUPPORTED fresh run.
  - The design removes the middle condition.
  - After a LOCALLY_MINIMAL reduction, the eligible default is exactly the neighbour the reducer already saw at 0/3. So diagnosis becomes a repeat of reduction, and POLICY_GAP becomes close to automatic for any reduced source.
- It removes the only path in the Learn loop by which a real evidence-gap source can avoid a POLICY_GAP label.
  - validate_gap is used only in tests (diagnostics.py:84-102).
  - Every option only weakens or removes the fault, and removing the fault also clears an evidence-gap violation.
  - So evidence-gap sources would be labelled POLICY_GAP and would spend candidate money.
- It makes the stored record say something false.
  - For a FIXED_DEFAULT diagnosis, classify_policy_gap still writes the fixed explanation 'Fresh reproduction and the declared controlled intervention support a bounded policy hypothesis.' (diagnostics.py:81).
  - The design's own fixed hypothesis, however, says 'No explanation of the agent's failure is claimed.'
  - The design refuses to edit diagnostics.py (to keep checker_hash), so it cannot fix that sentence.
  - experiment-protocol.md:90-96 requires an intervention 'supporting the stated recovery hypothesis'. Under this design there is none.
- Its choices depend on outcomes.
  - The option is picked by its earlier reduction results. The fresh trials protect the verdict from that selection.
  - More seriously, the design is judged by turning the two lost dev-5 diagnoses into POLICY_GAP (2/4 to 4/4). That is raising a gate's pass rate on a known source.

3. Smaller issues.
- After invalid output, the record would carry proposed_kind 'INCONCLUSIVE' (the code default, diagnosis.py:149) next to kind POLICY_GAP, and the candidate Mechanic sees both (learning.py:259).
- The fixed text lands in InterventionExperiment.hypothesis, which DiagnosticPanel shows as the model's hypothesis. The frontend change that would label it is marked optional; it must be mandatory.
- Eligibility uses observed_outcomes' looser idea of a valid trial (diagnosis.py:114-119).
- Dashboards could hide Mechanic regressions unless every report splits results by selected_by.
blocking_concerns: Makes a gate easier: removes the condition that a valid Mechanic answer must request an intervention before POLICY_GAP can be reached. After a LOCALLY_MINIMAL reduction the default is the neighbour already seen at 0/3, so POLICY_GAP becomes close to automatic and diagnosis just repeats reduction.

Removes the only Learn-loop path by which a real evidence-gap source avoids a POLICY_GAP label. validate_gap is test-only (diagnostics.py:84-102), and removing the fault also clears evidence-gap violations, so evidence-gap sources would be labelled POLICY_GAP and sent to candidate spend.

The record would contain a false statement. For FIXED_DEFAULT diagnoses the unchanged classify_policy_gap still writes 'Fresh reproduction and the declared controlled intervention support a bounded policy hypothesis.' (diagnostics.py:81), while the fixed hypothesis disclaims any explanation. The design will not edit diagnostics.py, so this cannot be fixed, and POLICY_GAP would carry no recovery hypothesis, against experiment-protocol.md:90-96.
Needs the owner to accept a written-protocol amendment (experiment-protocol.md:82-83 and the design line at diagnosis.py:1). It cannot ship without that acceptance.
Motivated by outcomes: its stated benefit is raising dev-5 POLICY_GAP from 2/4 to 4/4 on the same known source, i.e. increasing a gate's pass rate rather than making it more correct.

Records and dashboards would mislead unless changed: proposed_kind 'INCONCLUSIVE' next to kind POLICY_GAP, and fixed text shown in DiagnosticPanel as the model's hypothesis. The frontend labelling marked optional must be mandatory.

scores.title: Minimal change: one declared, fixed 'diagnosis_guide' block (kind definitions, public check meanings, task text, length rule) added to Mechanic diagnosis requests in new Learn plans only
scores.reasons:
1. Fixed code still decides the verdict, and no gate changes.
- Only fixed text is added to the diagnosis request, through a wrapper in the same pattern as CitationStatusMechanic (learning.py:243-244).
- mechanic.py, prompts/diagnosis.md, diagnosis.py and referee/diagnostics.py are left byte-identical, and so are the 600-character limit, the null and invalid paths (diagnosis.py:135,145,149) and the candidate gate (learning.py:250).
- This is the smallest change of the three, and it touches no gate-adjacent code.
- The only new refusal is a Start-time check that the frozen plan text matches (as at run_plans.py:996). That checks plan consistency, not scores.

2. The model gets no new episode information and no scoring advantage.
- block() takes only task_text, which is bound to the plan (runner.py:87) and sent to the agent (external_agent.py:315, via runner.py:165).
- The check meanings are the public PUBLIC_INVARIANTS text already given to the Explorer (explorer.py:21-30,284).
- Candidate requests get no block, and the diagnostic record passed to them has no hypothesis (learning.py:259).
- The diagnosis output has no scoring role (diagnostics.py:76-81).
- It contains no dev-5 example.

3. It is honest to declare.
- The text is frozen, the PUBLIC_INVARIANTS hash is checked, absent fields are omitted, and old plans keep their bytes.
- It keeps proposed_kind out of the success measures and pre-registers a paid probe judged on hypothesis content rather than on POLICY_GAP rate. That is good practice.

4. Deductions.
- (a) The designer says it left out facts that push the model toward requesting, but the 'use' text still says a null request or invalid output means 'no experiment runs and the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE'. That is the main source of such pressure, so the claim is only partly accurate. It is milder than Design 1's added 'not a claim of support' sentence.
- (b) The kind definitions and the sentence 'Contract here means the public service API ... not ... the adapter's evidence labels' were written after seeing the failure.
  - The designer admits this, and the text only changes model output that has no authority.
  - The POLICY_GAP definition ('a different recovery policy ... could plausibly prevent') could push the labels toward POLICY_GAP.
- (c) 'Where C6 passed, that report's citations met it' depends on C6's implementation matching its public text. That cannot be verified here because checks.py is off limits.
- (d) It does not fix the recorded-proposed_kind ambiguity (declined vs invalid vs code default) that produced the false run-doc line at docs/PRODUCT_NATIVE_V2_RUN_2026-09-29.md:393. Records stay as ambiguous as today: no worse, but no better.
- (e) Scope covers all new Learn plans, which confounds comparison with the 19 reference diagnoses.

5. Conditions before merging (not blockers).
- Update the tests that pin plan keys.
- Have someone authorised to read checks.py confirm that the C6 public meaning matches the implementation before the text is frozen.
